summary: Temporary cross-project GCP service account & limited AWS role access for data-migration runbook
description:
Issue summary: Platform migration task requires a temporary, auditable cross-project GCP service account with tightly scoped IAM permissions and a corresponding assume-role pattern in our AWS management account for datastore migration.

Impact: Without this access the migration team cannot run bulk datastore export/import jobs scheduled for 2026-03-14. The migration is time-sensitive because it coordinates with a downtime window for downstream analytics jobs.

Request: Create a GCP service account in project 'redwood-migration-2026' that can be impersonated from the engineering project 'redwood-core-prod' by a short-lived IAM binding. Grant the service account only the following roles: roles/storage.objectViewer (limited to the 'redwood-migration-exports' bucket), roles/pubsub.subscriber (to a single subscription arn:projects/redwood-migration-2026/subscriptions/migration-sync), and roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator scoped to the specific service account (so engineers can generate short-lived tokens). Additionally, in the AWS management account create an IAM role (ARN to be supplied) that allows sts:AssumeRole from a specified GCP workload identity (or from our cross-account OIDC provider) for temporary access to S3 staging bucket 'redwood-migration-staging' with s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject only.

Duration: Access should be time-limited to 72 hours from first use. Tokens/credentials must be rotated/revoked immediately after migration.

Justification: Required for migration coordination across clouds; avoids long-lived credentials and preserves audit trail via impersonation and STS. Security has signed off on principle; they require a pre-signed runbook and an audit tag on all resources created.

Acceptance criteria: 1) GCP service account exists and can be impersonated from redwood-core-prod only. 2) IAM bindings are least-privilege. 3) AWS role with trust to the GCP identity exists and can be assumed by a documented process. 4) Audit log entries show impersonation and AssumeRole events during a dry-run. 5) Access expires automatically after 72 hours or earlier via revocation instructions.

Requested by: Platform Migration squad (ticketed change window 2026-03-14 02:00-05:00 UTC).
steps_to_reproduce:
N/A - access provisioning task. Procedure to validate once created:
1) From redwood-core-prod project, run 'gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=sa-migration@redwood-migration-2026.iam.gserviceaccount.com' and confirm token returned.
2) Attempt gsutil ls gs://redwood-migration-exports with impersonation and confirm only allowed objects are visible.
3) From an ephemeral AWS role session, run 'aws s3 ls s3://redwood-migration-staging' and attempt a put/get to ensure policy scoping.
4) Verify Cloud Audit Logs show serviceAccountTokenCreator and storage.objectViewer events.
investigation_notes:
Security checked initial policy draft and requested removal of broad roles (no roles/storage.admin or roles/owner). Asked for explicit resource bindings (bucket-level) and logging labels. Oncall-ops recommended using Workload Identity Federation for AWS->GCP assumption flow where possible. IAM team proposed adding an additional condition limiting impersonation to principals with tag 'migration-run'=true. Engineering flagged that tooling (migration script) will be updated to set that tag during run.

Preliminary risks: - If tokenCreator is mis-scoped, tokens could be minted for other targets. - Cross-account trust misconfiguration could leave S3 bucket accessible; must test in dry-run.
